title: MAHARASHTRA CLASS 6 — Science | Physical Chemical Changes
description: Subject-wise test on Physical Chemical Changes (Science) for MAHARASHTRA CLASS 6. 25Q.
subject: maha6-science

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a physical change?

options.explanation: Burning of wood is a chemical change as it involves the formation of new substances like ash and carbon dioxide.
Rusting of iron is a chemical change as it involves the formation of a new substance, iron oxide.
Melting of ice is a physical change as it only changes the state of water from solid to liquid, without changing its chemical composition.
Cooking an egg is a chemical change as it involves the denaturation of proteins and the formation of new substances.

questions.explanation: Melting of ice only changes its state from solid to liquid, but its chemical composition (H2O) remains the same. No new substance is formed.
questions.subject: maha6-science

questions.question: In which type of change is a new substance formed with different chemical properties?

options.explanation: Physical changes do not involve the formation of new substances with different chemical properties.
Chemical changes involve the formation of new substances with different chemical properties.
Reversible changes can be either physical or chemical, but they do not necessarily involve the formation of new substances with different chemical properties.
Temporary changes are not a specific type of change, and they do not necessarily involve the formation of new substances with different chemical properties.

questions.explanation: Chemical changes are characterized by the formation of one or more new substances that have different chemical compositions and properties from the original substances.
questions.subject: maha6-science

questions.question: Tearing a sheet of paper into smaller pieces is an example of a:

options.explanation: Chemical changes involve the formation of new substances with different chemical properties, which is not the case when tearing paper.

Physical changes involve a change in the physical state or properties of a substance, without changing its chemical composition. Tearing paper is a physical change as it only alters the size and shape of the paper.
Irreversible changes are changes that cannot be reversed, but tearing paper is not necessarily an irreversible change, as the pieces can be taped back together.
Permanent changes are changes that are lasting and cannot be reversed, but tearing paper is not necessarily a permanent change, as the pieces can be taped back together.

questions.explanation: Tearing paper only alters its size and shape, but the paper itself remains chemically the same. No new substance is formed.
questions.subject: maha6-science

questions.question: Which of the following is typically a characteristic indicator of a chemical change?

options.explanation: Changes in shape can occur in both physical and chemical changes, and are not a specific indicator of a chemical change.
Changes in state (such as melting or boiling) are physical changes, and are not a specific indicator of a chemical change.
The formation of gas (like bubbles during a reaction between baking soda and lemon juice) is a common visual indicator that a new gaseous substance has been produced, signifying a chemical change.
Changes in size can occur in both physical and chemical changes, and are not a specific indicator of a chemical change.

questions.explanation: While physical changes can involve changes in shape, state, or size, the formation of gas (like bubbles during a reaction between baking soda and lemon juice) is a common visual indicator that a new gaseous substance has been produced, signifying a chemical change.
questions.subject: maha6-science

questions.question: Which of these processes is *not* considered a chemical change?

options.explanation: Digestion of food is a chemical change as it involves the breakdown of complex molecules into simpler ones through chemical reactions.
Rusting of an iron gate is a chemical change as it involves the formation of a new substance, iron oxide.
Dissolving sugar in water is a physical change as the sugar molecules disperse in water but retain their chemical identity; they can be recovered by evaporating the water.
Burning of a magnesium ribbon is a chemical change as it involves the formation of new substances, such as magnesium oxide.

questions.explanation: Digestion, rusting, and burning all involve chemical reactions that form new substances. Dissolving sugar in water is a physical change where sugar molecules disperse in water but retain their chemical identity; they can be recovered by evaporating the water.
questions.subject: maha6-science

questions.question: A student mixes baking soda with lemon juice. They observe bubbles being formed. This observation most strongly indicates:

options.explanation: Physical changes do not typically involve the formation of new substances, such as the gas bubbles observed in this reaction.
The formation of gas bubbles (carbon dioxide) when baking soda reacts with lemon juice is a clear sign that a new substance has been formed through a chemical reaction.
The formation of bubbles does not necessarily indicate a change in temperature.

options.text: The substances have only changed their state.
options.explanation: The formation of bubbles indicates the formation of a new substance, not just a change in state.

questions.explanation: The formation of gas bubbles (carbon dioxide) when baking soda reacts with lemon juice is a clear sign that a new substance has been formed through a chemical reaction.
questions.subject: maha6-science

questions.question: When a candle burns, both physical and chemical changes occur simultaneously. Which of the following represents the chemical change?

options.explanation: Melting of wax is a physical change as it only involves a change in the state of the wax, without changing its chemical composition.
Solidification of wax is a physical change as it only involves a change in the state of the wax, without changing its chemical composition.

options.text: Burning of wax to produce carbon dioxide and water vapour
options.explanation: The actual burning (combustion) of the wax involves it reacting with oxygen to form new substances like carbon dioxide and water vapour, which is a chemical change.

options.text: Change in the shape of the candle
options.explanation: A change in the shape of the candle is a physical change, and does not necessarily involve the formation of new substances.

questions.explanation: Melting and solidification of wax are physical changes as the wax's chemical composition doesn't change. The actual burning (combustion) of the wax involves it reacting with oxygen to form new substances like carbon dioxide and water vapour, which is a chemical change.
questions.subject: maha6-science

questions.question: You observe that an apple slice, when left exposed to air for some time, turns brown. This browning is an example of a:

options.text: Physical change, as its shape remains the same.
options.explanation: Physical changes do not typically involve the formation of new substances, such as the brown-colored compounds observed in this reaction.

options.text: Chemical change, as a new substance is formed.
options.explanation: The browning of an apple is caused by the oxidation of certain compounds in the apple by oxygen in the air, forming new, brown-colored substances.

options.text: Physical change, as it can be reversed by adding water.
options.explanation: The browning of an apple is an irreversible chemical change, and cannot be reversed by adding water.

options.text: Chemical change, as it melts due to heat.
options.explanation: The browning of an apple is not caused by melting due to heat, but rather by the oxidation of certain compounds in the apple by oxygen in the air.

questions.explanation: The browning of an apple is caused by the oxidation of certain compounds in the apple by oxygen in the air. This process forms new, brown-colored substances and is an irreversible chemical change.

questions.question: Assertion (A): Melting of ice to form water is a physical change. Reason (R): During melting, the chemical composition of water changes.

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: Reason (R) is false, as the chemical composition of water does not change during melting.

options.text: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: Reason (R) is false, as the chemical composition of water does not change during melting.

options.text: A is true, but R is false.
options.explanation: Assertion (A) is true because melting ice only changes its state (solid to liquid), but the substance remains water (H2O). Reason (R) is false because the chemical composition of water (H2O) does not change during melting.

options.text: A is false, but R is true.
options.explanation: Assertion (A) is true, and Reason (R) is false, as the chemical composition of water does not change during melting.

questions.explanation: Assertion (A) is true because melting ice only changes its state (solid to liquid), but the substance remains water (H2O). Reason (R) is false because the chemical composition of water (H2O) does not change during melting; only the arrangement and energy of its molecules change.

questions.question: A scientist performs two experiments. In Experiment 1, she heats a beaker of water until it boils and steam is produced. In Experiment 2, she places an iron nail in a solution of copper sulphate, and after some time, observes a reddish-brown deposit on the nail and the blue colour of the solution fades. Identify the types of changes in Experiment 1 and Experiment 2, respectively.

options.text: Experiment 1: Chemical change; Experiment 2: Physical change
options.explanation: Experiment 1 is a physical change, and Experiment 2 is a chemical change.

options.text: Experiment 1: Physical change; Experiment 2: Chemical change
options.explanation: In Experiment 1, boiling water into steam is a physical change. In Experiment 2, the iron nail reacts with copper sulphate to form new substances, which is a chemical change.

options.text: Experiment 1: Chemical change; Experiment 2: Chemical change
options.explanation: Experiment 1 is a physical change, and Experiment 2 is a chemical change.

options.text: Experiment 1: Physical change; Experiment 2: Physical change
options.explanation: Experiment 1 is a physical change, but Experiment 2 is a chemical change.

questions.explanation: In Experiment 1, boiling water into steam is a change of state (liquid to gas), which is a physical change because water remains H2O. In Experiment 2, the iron nail reacts with copper sulphate to form iron sulphate and copper metal (the reddish-brown deposit). This is a chemical change as new substances are formed, and the colour of the solution also changes.

questions.question: What type of change occurs when ice melts into water?

options.explanation: Chemical changes involve the formation of new substances, which is not the case when ice melts.
Permanent changes are not a standard classification of changes in science.
Physical changes involve a change in state or properties of a substance without changing its chemical composition.
Irreversible changes are those that cannot be easily reversed, which is not a characteristic of melting ice.

questions.explanation: Melting of ice is a physical change because only the state of water changes from solid to liquid, but no new substance is formed. The chemical composition remains H₂O.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a chemical change?

options.explanation: Boiling water is a physical change because it involves a change of state from liquid to gas.
Rusting of iron is a chemical change because it involves the formation of a new substance with different properties.
Tearing paper is a physical change because it involves a change in shape or size, but not a change in chemical composition.
Dissolving sugar in water is a physical change because it involves the dispersion of sugar molecules in water, but not the formation of a new substance.

questions.explanation: Rusting of iron is a chemical change because iron reacts with oxygen and moisture to form a new substance, iron oxide (rust), which has different properties from iron.

questions.question: When you light a matchstick, it burns and produces ash and smoke. This is an example of:

options.explanation: Physical changes do not involve the formation of new substances.
Chemical changes involve the formation of new substances and the release of energy, which is the case when a matchstick burns.
Reversible changes are those that can be easily reversed, which is not the case when a matchstick burns.
Changes of state involve a change from one state of matter to another, but do not involve the formation of new substances.

questions.explanation: Burning a matchstick produces new substances (ash, smoke, gases) and releases heat and light, which are characteristics of a chemical change.

options.explanation: Formation of new substances is a characteristic of chemical changes, not physical changes.
Irreversible nature is not a characteristic of physical changes, which are often reversible.
Change in shape or size is a characteristic of physical changes, which involve alterations in appearance or state.

options.text: Release or absorption of a large amount of energy

questions.question: Which of the following changes is generally considered irreversible?

options.explanation: Melting of chocolate is a physical change and is reversible.
Freezing of water is a physical change and is reversible.
Stretching a rubber band is a physical change and is reversible, to some extent.
Burning of paper is a chemical change and is generally considered irreversible, as the paper cannot be easily converted back into its original form.

questions.explanation: Burning paper is a chemical change that produces ash and smoke, and these new substances cannot be easily converted back into paper. Therefore, it is irreversible.

questions.question: Which statement is TRUE about a physical change?

options.text: A new substance with different properties is formed.

options.text: The chemical composition of the substance changes.

options.text: It is usually reversible and no new substance is formed.

questions.question: Consider the following statements: I. Dissolving sugar in water is a chemical change. II. Burning of wood is an irreversible change. III. In a physical change, the molecular structure of the substance remains the same. Which of the above statements is/are INCORRECT?

options.explanation: Only statement I is incorrect because dissolving sugar in water is a physical change, not a chemical change.
Statement II is correct, so it is not the incorrect statement.
Statement II is correct, so it is not one of the incorrect statements.
Statement III is correct, so it is not one of the incorrect statements.

questions.explanation: Statement I is INCORRECT: Dissolving sugar in water is a physical change because sugar can be recovered by evaporating the water, and no new substance is formed. Statement II is CORRECT: Burning of wood is a chemical change that produces ash, smoke, and gases, and it cannot be reversed to get the wood back. Hence, it is irreversible. Statement III is CORRECT: In a physical change, the molecules themselves do not change; only their arrangement or spacing changes.
